items.stem: If a circle can be inscribed in a parallelogram how will the parallelogram change?
items.answer: For a parallelogram circumscribing a circle the tangent lengths force each pair of adjacent sides to be equal, so all four sides become equal and the angles become right angles. The parallelogram therefore changes into a rectangle or a square.

items.stem: What is the maximum number of parallel tangents a circle can have on a diameter?
items.answer: A tangent touches a circle at exactly one point, and the only tangents perpendicular to a given diameter are the ones drawn at its two end points. Hence a circle can have at most two parallel tangents on a diameter.

items.stem: Prove that in two concentric circles, the chord of the larger circle, which touches the smaller circle is bisected at the point of contact.
items.answer: Let the two circles have the common centre O, and let AB be a chord of the larger circle that touches the smaller circle at P. OP is a radius of the smaller circle and AB is a tangent to it at P, so OP ⊥ AB. Now for the larger circle O is the centre and AB is a chord with OP ⊥ AB, and the perpendicular drawn from the centre to a chord bisects the chord. Hence AP = PB, that is, the chord is bisected at the point of contact. Hence proved.

items.stem: In figure, a circle touches all the four sides of a quadrilateral ABCD. If AB = 6 cm, BC = 9 cm and CD = 8 cm, then find the length of AD.
items.answer: Let the circle touch AB, BC, CD and DA at P, Q, R and S respectively. Tangents from an external point are equal, so let AP = AS = x. Then BP = AB − AP = 6 − x and BQ = BP = 6 − x. Next CQ = BC − BQ = 9 − (6 − x) = 3 + x and CR = CQ = 3 + x. Then RD = CD − CR = 8 − (3 + x) = 5 − x and DS = RD = 5 − x. Therefore AD = AS + SD = x + (5 − x) = 5. Thus AD = 5 cm.

items.stem: Prove that the lengths of two tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal.
items.answer: Let the circle have centre O and radius r, and let two tangents from an external point P touch it at A and B. Join OA, OB and OP. In triangles PAO and PBO, OP is common and OA = OB = r, being radii of the same circle. A radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact, so ∠OAP = ∠OBP = 90° and both triangles are right angled. By the RHS congruence rule ΔPAO ≅ ΔPBO, and hence AP = BP. Thus the two tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal in length. Hence proved.

items.stem: Prove that tangents drawn at the ends of a chord of a circle make equal angles with the chord.
items.answer: Let MN be a chord of the circle and let the tangents at M and N meet at the external point P. The two tangents from P are equal, so PM = PN. In triangle PMN the angles opposite these equal sides are equal, so ∠1 = ∠2, where ∠1 and ∠2 are the angles the tangents make with the chord on the side of P. The angles ∠3 and ∠4 on the other side of the chord form linear pairs with ∠1 and ∠2, so 180° − ∠1 = 180° − ∠2 gives ∠3 = ∠4. Hence the tangents at the ends of a chord make equal angles with the chord. Hence proved.

items.stem: A circle touches the side BC of a ΔABC at a point P and touches AB and AC when produced at Q and R respectively. Show that AQ = ½ (Perimeter of ΔABC).
items.answer: Tangent segments drawn to a circle from the same external point are equal. From A, AQ = AR; from B, BQ = BP; from C, CP = CR. Now the perimeter of ΔABC is AB + BC + AC = AB + BP + PC + AC = AB + BQ + CR + AC = AQ + AR = 2AQ, using BP = BQ, PC = CR and then AQ = AR. Hence AQ = ½ × Perimeter of ΔABC.

items.stem: If tangents PA and PB drawn from an external point P to a circle with centre O are inclined to each other at an angle of 80°, then find ∠POA.
items.answer: PA and PB are tangents from the same external point, so PO bisects ∠APB. Hence ∠APO = 80° ÷ 2 = 40°. OA is a radius and PA is the tangent at A, so ∠PAO = 90°. In ΔAPO the angles add to 180°, so ∠PAO + ∠APO + ∠POA = 180°, i.e. 90° + 40° + ∠POA = 180°. Therefore ∠POA = 50°.

items.stem: An isosceles triangle ABC, with AB = AC, circumscribes a circle, touching BC at P, AC at Q and AB at R. Prove that the contact point P bisects BC.
items.answer: Tangents drawn from an external point are equal, so AR = AQ, BR = BP and CP = CQ. Since AB = AC, we may write AR + BR = AQ + CQ. Replacing BR by BP and CQ by CP gives AR + BP = AQ + CP, and since AR = AQ this reduces to BP = CP. Therefore the point of contact P bisects BC.

items.stem: Prove that the rectangle circumscribing a circle is a square.
items.answer: Let rectangle ABCD circumscribe a circle, touching AB at P, BC at Q, CD at R and DA at S. Tangents from an external point are equal, so AP = AS, PB = BQ, DR = DS and RC = QC. Adding these four equations gives AP + PB + DR + RC = AS + SD + BQ + QC, that is AB + CD = AD + BC. In a rectangle AB = CD and AD = BC, so 2AB = 2BC, giving AB = BC. A rectangle whose adjacent sides are equal is a square, so ABCD is a square.

items.stem: Prove that the tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact.
items.answer: Let the circle have centre O and let AB be the tangent touching it at P. Take any other point Q on AB and join OQ, meeting the circle at R. Then OP = OR, both being radii, and OQ = OR + RQ, so OQ > OR, that is OQ > OP. Since Q was any point of AB other than P, OP is shorter than every other segment joining O to a point of AB. The shortest segment from a point to a line is the perpendicular, so OP ⊥ AB. Hence the tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact.

items.stem: If a circle touches the side BC of a triangle ABC at P and extended sides AB and AC at Q and R respectively, prove that AQ = ½(BC + CA + AB).
items.answer: Tangent segments from the same external point are equal: from B, BQ = BP; from A, AQ = AR; from C, CP = CR. Now AB + BC + CA = (AQ − BQ) + (BP + PC) + (AR − CR) = (AQ − BQ) + (BQ + CR) + (AQ − CR) = 2AQ. Hence AQ = ½(BC + CA + AB).

By the angle sum property of ΔTPQ, (90° − θ) + (90° − θ) + ∠PTQ = 180°, so ∠PTQ = 2θ. Hence ∠PTQ = 2∠OPQ.

items.stem: A circle is inscribed in a ΔABC, with sides AC, AB and BC as 8 cm, 10 cm and 12 cm respectively. Find the length of AD, BE and CF.
items.answer: The inscribed circle touches AB at D, BC at E and CA at F. Let AF = x. Tangents from an external point are equal, so at A, AF = AD = x; at B, BE = BD = AB − AD = 10 − x; at C, CE = CF = AC − AF = 8 − x. Now BC = BE + EC, so 12 = (10 − x) + (8 − x), giving 2x = 18 − 12 = 6 and x = 3. Hence AD = 3 cm, BE = 10 − 3 = 7 cm and CF = 8 − 3 = 5 cm.

items.stem: Prove that the tangents drawn at the ends of a diameter of a circle are parallel.
items.answer: Let AB be a diameter of the circle and let CD and EF be the tangents drawn at A and B respectively. A tangent is perpendicular to the radius, and hence to the diameter, at its point of contact, so AB ⊥ CD and AB ⊥ EF. Therefore ∠CAB = 90° and ∠ABF = 90°, so ∠CAB = ∠ABF; similarly ∠ABE = ∠BAD. These are pairs of alternate interior angles formed by the lines CD and EF with the transversal AB, and they are equal, so CD ∥ EF. Hence the tangents at the ends of a diameter are parallel.

items.stem: In Figure, PQ is a chord of length 8 cm of a circle of radius 5 cm and centre O. The tangents at P and Q intersect at point T. Find the length of TP.
items.answer: Let OT meet the chord PQ at R. The two tangents TP and TQ from the external point T are equal, so OT is the perpendicular bisector of PQ. Hence PR = QR = 4 cm and ∠ORP = 90°. In right ΔORP, OR² = OP² − PR² = 5² − 4² = 9, so OR = 3 cm. In right ΔPRT, TP² = TR² + PR² = TR² + 16. In right ΔOPT, OT² = TP² + OP², so (TR + 3)² = TR² + 16 + 25, giving TR² + 6·TR + 9 = TR² + 41, so 6·TR = 32 and TR = 16/3 cm. Therefore TP² = (16/3)² + 4² = 256/9 + 16 = 400/9, and TP = 20/3 cm.

items.stem: A right triangle ABC, right angled at A is circumscribing a circle. If AB = 6 cm and BC = 10 cm, find the radius r of the circle.
items.answer: BC is the hypotenuse, so by Pythagoras AC = √(BC² − AB²) = √(10² − 6²) = √(100 − 36) = 8 cm. The area of the right triangle is ½ × AB × AC = ½ × 6 × 8 = 24 cm². Joining the incentre O to A, B and C splits ΔABC into ΔOBC, ΔOCA and ΔOAB, each of height r, so 24 = ½r(BC + AC + AB) = ½r(10 + 8 + 6) = 12r. Hence r = 2 cm.

items.stem: a, b and c are the sides of a right triangle, where c is the hypotenuse. A circle, of radius r, touches the sides of the triangle. Prove that r = (a + b − c)/2.
items.answer: Let the right angle be at C, with CB = a, CA = b and AB = c, and let the incircle with centre O touch CB at M, CA at N and AB at P. A radius is perpendicular to the tangent at its point of contact, so OM ⟂ CB and ON ⟂ CA; together with the right angle at C, the quadrilateral OMCN has three right angles, and OM = ON = r, so OMCN is a square. Hence CM = CN = r. Tangents from an external point are equal, so AN = AP and BM = BP. From AN = AP, AC − CN = AB − BP, that is b − r = c − BM = c − (a − r) = c − a + r. Therefore b − r = c − a + r, so 2r = a + b − c and r = (a + b − c)/2. Hence proved.

items.stem: Prove that opposite sides of a quadrilateral circumscribing a circle subtend supplementary angles at the centre of the circle.
items.answer: Let the circle with centre O be inscribed in quadrilateral ABCD, touching AB at E, BC at H, CD at G and DA at F. Join O to A, B, C, D and to E, F, G, H. Number the eight angles at O in order: ∠1 = ∠AOE, ∠2 = ∠EOB, ∠3 = ∠BOH, ∠4 = ∠HOC, ∠5 = ∠COG, ∠6 = ∠GOD, ∠7 = ∠DOF, ∠8 = ∠FOA. In ΔAEO and ΔAFO, OE = OF (radii), ∠OEA = ∠OFA = 90° (radius perpendicular to tangent) and OA is common, so ΔAEO ≅ ΔAFO and hence ∠1 = ∠8. In the same way ∠2 = ∠3, ∠4 = ∠5 and ∠6 = ∠7. The angles round the point O add to 360°, so ∠1 + ∠2 + ∠3 + ∠4 + ∠5 + ∠6 + ∠7 + ∠8 = 360°, which becomes 2∠1 + 2∠2 + 2∠5 + 2∠6 = 360°, so ∠1 + ∠2 + ∠5 + ∠6 = 180°. But ∠1 + ∠2 = ∠AOB and ∠5 + ∠6 = ∠COD, hence ∠AOB + ∠COD = 180°. Similarly ∠BOC + ∠AOD = 180°. So opposite sides subtend supplementary angles at the centre. Hence proved.

items.stem: Prove that tangent drawn at any point of a circle perpendicular to the radius through the point contact.
items.answer: Let AB be a tangent to a circle with centre O touching it at the point P. Take any other point Q on AB and join OQ. Since Q lies outside the circle, OQ meets the circle at some point R between O and Q, so OQ = OR + RQ > OR. But OR = OP because both are radii, hence OQ > OP. This holds for every point Q on AB other than P, so OP is the shortest segment from O to the line AB. The shortest segment from a point to a line is the perpendicular to that line, therefore OP ⟂ AB. That is, the tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact. Hence proved.

items.stem: AB is a chord of circle with centre O. At B, a tangent PB is drawn such that its length is 24 cm. The distance of P from the centre is 26 cm. If the chord AB is 16 cm, find its distance from the centre.
items.answer: PB is a tangent at B and OB is the radius to the point of contact, so ∠OBP = 90° and ΔOPB is right angled at B. Hence OB = √(OP² − BP²) = √(26² − 24²) = √(676 − 576) = √100 = 10 cm, which is the radius. Let OC be the perpendicular from O to the chord AB. A perpendicular drawn from the centre bisects the chord, so BC = ½ × AB = 16/2 = 8 cm. In right ΔOCB, OC² = OB² − BC² = 10² − 8² = 100 − 64 = 36, so OC = 6 cm. The distance of the chord from the centre is 6 cm.

items.stem: From a point T outside a circle of centre O, tangents TP and TQ are drawn to the circle. Prove that OT is the right bisector of line segment PQ.
items.answer: Let OT cut PQ at R. Tangents drawn from an external point are equal in length, so TP = TQ. In ΔTPQ the sides TP and TQ are equal, so the angles opposite them are equal: ∠TPR = ∠TQR. Now compare ΔPTR and ΔQTR: TP = TQ, ∠TPR = ∠TQR and TR is common, so ΔPTR ≅ ΔQTR by SAS. By CPCT, PR = QR and ∠PRT = ∠QRT. Since PQ is a straight segment, ∠PRT + ∠QRT = 180°, and as the two are equal each is 90°. Thus OT passes through the midpoint of PQ and is perpendicular to it, so OT is the right bisector of PQ. Hence proved.

items.stem: In Figure, PQ and RS are two parallel tangents to a circle with centre O and another tangent AB with point of contact C intersecting PQ at A and RS at B. Prove that ∠AOB = 90°.
items.answer: Let PQ touch the circle at D and RS touch it at E. From the external point A the tangents AD and AC are drawn, so DA = AC. A radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact, so ∠ODA = ∠OCA = 90°, and OD = OC as radii. Hence ΔDOA ≅ ΔCOA (RHS / SAS), and by CPCT ∠DOA = ∠COA. In the same way, from B the tangents BE and BC give ΔBOC ≅ ΔBOE, so ∠COB = ∠BOE. Now PQ ∥ RS and both touch the circle, so D, O and E are collinear and DOE is a straight line. The angles on this straight line at O add to 180°: ∠DOA + ∠AOC + ∠COB + ∠BOE = 180°. Using the two equalities, 2∠AOC + 2∠COB = 180°, so ∠AOC + ∠COB = 90°. But ∠AOC + ∠COB = ∠AOB, therefore ∠AOB = 90°. Hence proved.

items.stem: Prove that the parallelogram circumscribing a circle is a rhombus.
items.answer:
Let ABCD be a parallelogram circumscribing a circle, touching AB at P, BC at Q, CD at R and DA at S.
Since ABCD is a parallelogram, AB = CD and AD = BC.  …(1)
The lengths of tangents drawn from an external point are equal, so
at A: AP = AS,  at B: BP = BQ,  at C: CR = CQ,  at D: DR = DS.
Adding these four equalities,
AP + PB + CR + DR = AS + BQ + CQ + DS
Grouping the pieces along each side gives AB + CD = AD + BC.
Using (1), 2AB = 2AD, so AB = AD.
A parallelogram with two adjacent sides equal has all four sides equal. Therefore ABCD is a rhombus. Hence proved.

items.stem: In given figure, PA and PB are tangents from a point P to the circle with centre O. At the point M, other tangent to the circle is drawn cutting PA and PB at K and N. Prove that the perimeter of ΔPNK = 2PB.
items.answer:
Tangents drawn to a circle from an external point are equal in length, so
PA = PB (from P), KM = KA (from K) and MN = BN (from N).
Now KN = KM + MN = KA + BN.
The perimeter of ΔPNK is
p = PN + KN + PK
 = PN + BN + KA + PK
 = (PN + NB) + (PK + KA)
 = PB + PA
 = 2PB, since PA = PB.
Therefore the perimeter of ΔPNK = 2PB. Hence proved.

items.stem: In the figure, tangents PQ and PR are drawn from an external point P to a circle with centre O, such that ∠RPQ = 30°. A chord RS is drawn parallel to the tangent PQ. Find ∠RQS.
items.answer:
Tangents from an external point are equal, so PR = PQ and ΔPQR is isosceles.
Its base angles are therefore equal:
∠PRQ = ∠PQR = (180° − 30°)/2 = 150°/2 = 75°
Since SR ∥ QP, the angles ∠SRQ and ∠RQP are alternate angles, so
∠SRQ = ∠RQP = 75°
In ΔSQR this makes SQ = RQ, so the angles opposite them are equal:
∠RSQ = ∠SRQ = 75°
By the angle sum of ΔSQR,
∠SQR + 75° + 75° = 180°
∠SQR = 180° − 150° = 30°
Therefore ∠RQS = 30°.

items.stem: In the figure AB and CD are common tangents to two circles of unequal radii. Prove that AB = CD.
items.answer:
Extend AB and CD so that they meet at a point P; they do meet because the two circles have unequal radii.
From the external point P, PA and PC are tangents to the larger circle, so
PA = PC
Also from P, PB and PD are tangents to the smaller circle, so
PB = PD
Subtracting the second equality from the first,
PA − PB = PC − PD
But PA − PB = AB and PC − PD = CD.
Therefore AB = CD. Hence proved.

items.stem: In figure PQ is a tangent from an external point P to a circle with centre O and OP cuts the circle at T and ∠QOR is a diameter. If ∠POR = 130° and S is a point on the circle, find ∠1 + ∠2.

A radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact, so ∠OQP = 90°.
T lies on OP, so the central angle standing on arc TR is ∠TOR = ∠POR = 130°.
The angle subtended at the centre is twice the angle subtended at the circumference by the same arc, so at S
∠2 = ½ ∠TOR = ½ ∠POR = ½ × 130° = 65°
QOR is a diameter, so ∠QOR = 180° and
∠POQ = 180° − 130° = 50°
In ΔOQP the angles add to 180°:
∠1 = 180° − ∠OQP − ∠POQ = 180° − 90° − 50° = 40°
Therefore ∠1 + ∠2 = 65° + 40° = 105°.

items.stem: In the given figure, AD is a diameter of a circle with centre O and AB is a tangent at A. C is a point on the circle such that DC produced intersects the tangent at B and ∠ABC = 50°. Find ∠AOC.
items.answer:
A tangent drawn at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact, so at A
∠A = ∠OAB = 90°
In ΔDAB the angles add to 180°:
∠D + ∠A + ∠B = 180°
∠D + 90° + 50° = 180°
∠D = 40°
The angle subtended by an arc at the centre is twice the angle it subtends at the circumference, and ∠ADC = ∠D stands on arc AC. So
∠AOC = 2∠ADC = 2 × 40° = 80°
Therefore ∠AOC = 80°.

items.stem: In the given figure, PA and PB are tangents to the circle from an external point P. CD is another tangent touching the circle at Q. If PA = 12 cm, QC = QD = 3 cm, then find PC + PD.
items.answer:
Tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal in length, so
from C: CA = CQ = 3 cm
from D: DQ = DB = 3 cm
from P: PB = PA = 12 cm
Writing each of PA and PB in two pieces,
PA + PB = (PC + CA) + (PD + DB)
so PC + PD = PA − CA + PB − DB
 = 12 − 3 + 12 − 3
 = 18 cm
Therefore PC + PD = 18 cm.

items.stem:
A backyard is in the shape of a triangle ABC with right angle at B. AB = 7 m and BC = 15 m. A circular pit was dug inside it such that it touches the walls AC, BC and AB at P, Q and R respectively such that AP = x m.
Based on the above information, answer the following questions:
(i) Find the length of AR in terms of x.
(ii) Write the type of quadrilateral BQOR.
(iii) Find the length PC in terms of x and hence find the value of x.
(iv) Find x and hence find the radius r of circle.
items.answer:
(i) Tangents from an external point are equal, so from A: AR = AP = x m.
(ii) A radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact, so OR ⊥ AB and OQ ⊥ BC. Hence ∠ORB = ∠OQB = ∠RBQ = 90°, and by the angle sum of a quadrilateral ∠QOR = 360° − 90° − 90° − 90° = 90°. Also OR = OQ, both radii. So BQOR is a square.
(iii) By Pythagoras, AC = √(AB² + BC²) = √(7² + 15²) = √274 units, so PC = AC − AP = (√274 − x) units.
Also AR = AP = x, so BR = BQ = 7 − x, and CQ = PC = 15 − (7 − x) = x + 8.
Hence AC = AP + PC = x + x + 8 = 2x + 8, giving √274 = 2x + 8.
(iv) x = (√274 − 8)/2 m.
Since BQOR is a square, r = BR = 7 − x = 7 − (√274 − 8)/2 = (22 − √274)/2 m.
So x = (√274 − 8)/2 m and the radius r = (22 − √274)/2 m.

items.stem:
The picture given below shows a circular mirror hanging on the wall with a cord. The diagram represents the mirror as a circle with centre O. AP and AQ are tangents to the circle at P and Q respectively such that AP = 30 cm and ∠PAQ = 60°.
Based on the above information, answer the following questions :
(i) Find the length PQ.
(ii) Find m∠POQ.
(iii) Find the length OA.
(iv) Find the radius of the mirror.
items.answer:
Let M be the point where AO meets PQ. AO bisects ∠PAQ and is the perpendicular bisector of the chord PQ, so ∠PAM = 30° and ∠AMP = 90°.
(i) In ΔPAM, sin 30° = PM/AP, so ½ = PM/30, giving PM = 15 cm and PQ = 2PM = 30 cm.
(ii) In quadrilateral APOQ, ∠OPA = ∠OQA = 90° because a radius is perpendicular to the tangent, so
∠POQ + ∠OQA + ∠QAP + ∠APO = 360°
∠POQ + 90° + 60° + 90° = 360°
∠POQ + 240° = 360°, so m∠POQ = 120°.
(iii) In right ΔOAP, ∠OAP = 30° and cos 30° = AP/OA, so √3/2 = 30/OA, giving OA = 20√3 cm.
(iv) The radius is OP. In right ΔOAP, tan 30° = OP/AP, so 1/√3 = OP/30, giving OP = 10√3 cm.
So PQ = 30 cm, m∠POQ = 120°, OA = 20√3 cm and the radius of the mirror is 10√3 cm.

items.stem:
A children's park is in the triangular shape as shown in Figure below. In the middle of the park, there is a circular region for younger children to play. It is fenced with three layers of wire. The radius of the circular region is 3 m.
Based on the above, answer the following questions:
(i) Find the perimeter (or circumference) of the circular region.
(ii) What is the total length of wire used?
(iii) What is the area of the circular region?
(iv) If BD = 6 m, DC = 9 m and ar(ΔABC) = 54 m², then find the length of sides AB and AC, respectively.
(v) Find the perimeter of ΔABC.
items.answer:
(i) Perimeter of the circular region = 2πr = 2π × 3 = 6π m.
(ii) The fence has three layers, so the total wire = 3 × 6π = 18π m.
(iii) Area of the circular region = πr² = π(3)² = 9π m².
(iv) Let the circle touch AB at F, BC at D and CA at E. Tangents from a point are equal, so BF = BD = 6 m, CE = CD = 9 m; let AF = AE = x m. Then AB = x + 6, BC = 6 + 9 = 15 and AC = x + 9.
Splitting ΔABC into ΔAOB, ΔBOC and ΔAOC, each of height r = 3 m,
54 = ½ AB × OF + ½ BC × OD + ½ AC × OE
54 = ½(6 + x)(3) + ½(6 + 9)(3) + ½(9 + x)(3)
54 = (3/2)[6 + x + 15 + 9 + x]
36 = 2x + 30, so x = 3.
Hence AB = x + 6 = 9 m and AC = x + 9 = 12 m.
(v) Perimeter of ΔABC = AB + BC + AC = 9 + 15 + 12 = 36 m.
